raw:
Yewyn Corrford married Kadan Corrley at Kelmere, and the couple lived in Kelmere from then on (Excerpt 1002). Later mentions, such as Kassa Stenson going to live in Staveford and Rorald Lindmere going to Salcombe, concern other people. Nothing later moves Yewyn.

Answer: Kelmere

Luena Stenenridge's household started out in the harbor town of Dunstead (Chapter 1). The latest excerpt that places her anywhere is in Chapter 5, which opens "In the hill farms of Staveford" and then shows her watching the clouds there. Her son's later move to Ostcombe (Chapter 28) is only his own residence. Nothing says Luena moved there with him.

Answer: Staveford

Fewyn Stenworth's household was in Torton at the start. The latest move recorded for Fewyn is in Chapter 34: packed a single trunk and moved from Gulhaven to Yarlby. Later excerpts (Chapters 36, 39) mention Fewyn but give no further move.

Answer: Yarlby

Havie Prydenridge was born at Elmhaven and lived in Ostcombe with the family early on. In Chapter 30's later material, Havie "found work in Dunby, moved there, and did not return to Staveford" (Chapter 39). Chapter 40 places Havie in the harbor town of Dunby, and nothing later shows a move away.

Answer: Dunby

Wenelle Lindmere married Rovus Prydenridge and first lived in Ostcombe. In Chapter 22 she "went along to live in Kelmere as well", and the births in Chapters 25 and 37 place the family in Kelmere. The claim that she drowned crossing the estuary is only gossip from Ismira Stenson. The moves to Salcombe and Yarlby concern her father, Rorald Lindmere, not her.

Answer: Kelmere

Rinelle Corrley was born at Elmhaven and married Kadrek Brackick, then lived in Kelford. Later, in Chapter 35, "Rinelle Corrley went along to live in Torton as well." After that, "Dalis left Torton and settled in Yarlby" is about a different person (Dalis), not Rinelle. The latest relevant information about Rinelle's residence is Torton.

Answer: Torton

Thizek Stenenridge's latest residence information is in Chapter 38: a daughter, Kamira Stenenridge, was born to Movie Prydenridge and Thizek Stenenridge, and "The family lived in Elmhaven." Nothing later gives a different place. An earlier line, "In Torton," is a location tag on an unrelated passage and does not say he moved.

Answer: Elmhaven

Lurald Stenworth lived in Kelford while married to Luwyn Brackick, then in Dunstead, where Ferald and Isvie were born and where he appears in Chapter 24. In Chapter 25 he has a son, Istho, with Nerine Prydenridge, and the family lives in Ostcombe. The Chapter 28 excerpt, set in Ostcombe, also mentions him. The later excerpts name no new home. The promise to carry a letter to Quenford is an errand, not a move.

Answer: Ostcombe

Pelde Stenworth lived in Torton throughout the record. She married Sebin Brackick there, the couple lived in Torton from then on, and their daughter Elvie Brackick's birth is also placed in Torton. Nothing later shows her moving away.

Answer: Torton

Gadrek Prydenridge lived in Ostcombe with his family in Chapter 1. In Chapter 29 he married the eldest daughter of Lura Haskick in the chapel at Ostcombe, and the record says the couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. Nothing later moves him elsewhere. A mention of the abbey at Gulhaven is only a letter's content, not a move.

Answer: Ostcombe

Pelde Stenson married Davus at Torton, and the couple lived there from then on. Later passages (Chapters 33 and 37) still place her in Torton, and nothing in the record says she moved away. Only her father, Matho Stenson, is recorded as moving to Elmhaven.

Answer: Torton

The excerpts record Yedan Corrford's death (Chapter 18), but none records the death of Nylia Corrford. Without a date for her death, I can't place Jotho Thornmere at that time.

Answer: unknown

Malis died in Chapter 7 (excerpt 686). Peten Haskick's moves: in Chapter 1 he lived in Dunstead. He moved from Dunstead to Staveford in Chapter 14, and later (Chapter 39) rode out of Quenford to Gulhaven. At Chapter 7, the latest known move was none yet, so he was still in Dunstead (the Staveford move came in Chapter 14).

Answer: Dunstead

Islan Thornmere died in Chapter 29 (Excerpt 1575), at Dungate.

Gadrek Prydenridge's residence: in Chapter 29 (Excerpt 1579), he married in the chapel at Ostcombe and the couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. Excerpt 1579 comes after Excerpt 1575 in the record, so at the time of Islan's death he was most likely still in Ostcombe, where he had lived all along (Chapter 1 and Chapter 7 place him there). Nothing indicates he moved elsewhere.

Answer: Ostcombe

The excerpts never record Ulrald Corrford's death, but the latest information about where Pelde Stenson lived is clear. She married Davus Stenworth at Torton and "the couple lived in Torton from then on." The daughter Dalis was also born into a family living in Torton. Nothing later says she moved.

Answer: Torton

The excerpts never record Pewyn Stenenridge's death, so there is no point in time to compare against Taric Corrley's moves. Pewyn appears alive in several scenes, and nothing later mentions a death.

Answer: unknown

The excerpts never say when Nelan Brackick died, so I used Rorald Lindmere's latest recorded residence instead. He started in Kelmere, then moved to Salcombe (Chapter 19), and later to Yarlby (Chapter 35). Chapter 40 still places him in Yarlby, and nothing records a later move.

Answer: Yarlby

Orrald Stenson, known as "Orrald the Younger", died of a festering wound in Chapter 8. Havie Prydenridge lived with her family in Ostcombe from Chapter 1. Nothing in the record says she moved away before Chapter 8, and she is still seen alongside her Ostcombe family in Chapter 7.

Answer: Ostcombe

The excerpts never record Marald Corrford's death. Yedan Corrford's death is recorded in Chapter 18, but Marald is only shown alive, in Chapters 10, 14 and 21. Without a death date for Marald, there is no point in time to place Pelde Stenworth against.

The latest information about Pelde Stenworth is that she married Sebin Brackick at Torton in Chapter 34 and the couple lived there from then on. That cannot be tied to Marald's death.

Answer: unknown

Ismira Stenson's death is only implied: the last chapter records her bone compass going to Matho Stenson, while the plague rumour about her was unfounded. Kassa Stenson is placed in Torton, living at home with her parents. No later passage records her moving. The "Kassa Brackick" who appears in Staveford and Kelmere has a different surname, so I treated her as a different person. The plain "Kassa" at Kelmere in Chapter 35 is ambiguous, so this answer rests on that reading.

Answer: Torton

Gazek Stenson died in Chapter 5. At that point Thizek Stenenridge was still living in the family home in the harbor town of Dunstead, where he was introduced as the eldest child in Chapter 1. His father Rozek moved to Wilwick only later, in Chapter 13, and Thizek's move to Elmhaven comes later still, in Chapter 38.

Answer: Dunstead

Havus Stenworth rode out of Torton and by the next market day was living in Gulhaven (Chapter 7). Ludrek Prydenridge died later, in Chapter 11. Havus was apprenticed anew as a weaver in Chapter 15, but no move is recorded, so Gulhaven is the latest known residence.

Answer: Gulhaven

Orrald Stenson married Harine Lindmere (Excerpt 99). Later, "Orrald the Younger died of a wound that festered at Torton" (Excerpt 710), which could be a different person (the younger), not Orrald Stenson, her husband. Excerpt 663 says "Orrald talked for weeks of going to Gulhaven, yet in the end stayed where he was", which suggests Orrald is still alive. No record shows that Orrald Stenson died, so the latest information is that Harine is married to Orrald Stenson.

Answer: Orrald Stenson

Zalis Corrley was first married to Gadan Corrley. That husband died of a long wasting sickness at Kelmere (Chapter 18). Later, in Chapter 26, Ferald and Zalis Corrley were wed at Dunstead. No later excerpt mentions a death or separation. The record gives only the first name Ferald, with no surname.

Answer: Ferald

Pelde Stenworth, daughter of Havus Stenworth, first married Gazek Stenson (Chapter 1). Later, in Chapter 34, she married Sebin Brackick at Torton. The record never says Gazek died. Even so, the latest marriage is the most recent information, so I take Sebin Brackick as her current spouse.

Answer: Sebin Brackick

Pelde Stenson, the daughter of Matho and Ismira, married Davus Stenworth at Torton in Chapter 8, and they had a daughter, Dalis Stenworth, in Chapter 15. Davus is still present with Pelde in Chapter 32 and nothing says he died or the marriage ended.

The later marriage of Pelde Stenworth to Sebin Brackick concerns a different person, Pelde Stenworth, not Pelde Stenson.

Answer: Davus Stenworth

Lura Haskick is introduced in Chapter 1 as the wife of Peten Haskick. Nothing later in the record says Peten died, that they separated, or that Lura remarried. The later mentions of Peten are routine ones, such as him walking the long way round and handing over the silver chalice, and they treat him as still living. The marriage therefore stands.

Answer: Peten Haskick

Excerpt 1002 says Kadan Corrley took Yewyn Corrford in marriage at Kelmere. No later excerpt mentions a death or a change of spouse.

Answer: Kadan Corrley

Havus Stenworth and Fewyn Stenworth were married at the start, with four children. Havus later moved to Gulhaven and changed trade, but nothing in the record says he separated from Fewyn or that she died. Later excerpts still show them together ("said Havus. 'A scandal,' agreed Fewyn Stenworth"). Havus moved back to Torton, and nothing says Fewyn died or that the marriage ended.

Answer: Fewyn Stenworth

Kadan Corrley married Yewyn Corrford at Kelmere before the spring was out (Chapter 16). Later excerpts show them still together: Yewyn Corrford speaks alongside Kadan in Chapter 19. No excerpt reports Yewyn's death or a separation.

Answer: Yewyn Corrford

Movie Prydenridge married the only son of Luena Stenenridge in Chapter 28. Later, in Chapter 38, a daughter was born to Movie Prydenridge and Thizek Stenenridge, and the family lived in Elmhaven. Thizek Stenenridge is therefore the spouse. The record gives no sign of a death or other change after that.

Answer: Thizek Stenenridge

Chapter 28: Havie and Isric Thornmere were wed at Ostcombe. Havie Prydenridge is the Havie in question (Chapter 40 still shows Havie Prydenridge with Isric, with no later change). No death or other change is recorded for Havie.

Answer: Havie Prydenridge

The record never says Ferald Stenworth married. He is introduced as the son of Luwyn Brackick and Lurald Stenworth, born in Dunstead. No later excerpt gives him a spouse, so he has no living spouse.

Answer: none

Yera Haskick is the eldest daughter of Lura and Peten Haskick. In Chapter 29, Gadrek Prydenridge married the eldest daughter of Lura Haskick in Ostcombe. The record shows no later change.

Answer: Gadrek Prydenridge

Movus Brackick, son of Kadrek Brackick and Rinelle Corrley, married Dalis Stenworth in the chapel at Yarlby (Chapter 39). Dalis later gave birth to their son Iszek Brackick (Chapter 40). Nothing in the record says either of them died or that the marriage ended.

Answer: Dalis Stenworth

Luena Stenenridge is introduced as the wife of Rozek Stenenridge in Chapter 1. Nothing later says either of them died or that they separated. The later scenes in Chapters 5, 9, 12, 13, 14 and 21 show them still together, with Rozek and Luena talking, exchanging gifts and sharing confidences.

In Chapter 37 Rozek Stenenridge is still around, buying a ribbon at the stall. The Chapter 28 wedding concerns Luena's only son, and it does not affect her own marriage.

Answer: Rozek Stenenridge

Bremira Corrford, daughter of Kassa Brackick and Ulrald Corrford, married Zavus Prydenridge at Dunstead in Chapter 25. Nothing later in the record mentions his death or any separation, so he is her spouse at the end.

Answer: Zavus Prydenridge

Excerpt 1091 (Chapter 18) states that Yedan Corrford died of a kick from a cart horse at Dunstead. Later excerpts show Yedan alive only in chapters before that (Chapter 14). Chapter 19 mentions "Yera" agreeing, which is a different name. No later information says he is alive.

Answer: no

Orrald Stenson was known as "Orrald the Younger" (Excerpt 227). In Chapter 8, "Orrald the Younger died of a wound that festered at Torton." Nothing later in the record contradicts this.

Answer: no

The record says in Chapter 5 that Gazek Stenson died of a wound that festered at Torton. Nothing later contradicts this.

Answer: no

Excerpt 1575 (Chapter 29) states that Islan Thornmere died of old age, quietly in sleep at Dungate. Later excerpts only mention other people, and Excerpt 1197 refers to "the eldest son of Islan Thornmere" without suggesting he is alive. Nothing in the record contradicts the death.

Answer: no

Gadan Corrley's wife is Zalis Corrley (Excerpt 40). Excerpt 1115 (Chapter 18) says the husband of Zalis Corrley died of a long wasting sickness at Kelmere, so Gadan died there. Later mentions of him, such as "the youngest son of Gadan Corrley" in Chapter 22, don't show he was still alive.

Answer: no

The rumor of Ismira Stenson's death by plague (Chapter 8) is unsupported gossip. Later records show her alive: she moves to Elmhaven in Chapter 24 and hums while scrubbing the step in Chapter 30. In Chapter 37, the bone compass "which Ismira Stenson had owned" went to Matho Stenson. This phrasing suggests a bequest after her death, so the latest relevant information points to her having died.

Answer: no

In Chapter 16, the record says "That spring, the coughing sickness took Nelan; he was buried at Kelford." Later excerpts mention Nelan's youngest son and other family members, but nothing says Nelan came back to life, so he is not alive at the end of the record.

Answer: no

No death of Ulrald Corrford is recorded anywhere in the material. His latest mentions have him alive: he fathered Rimor in Staveford (Chapter 20), and his silver flute passed to Kassa Brackick (Chapter 21). The flute transfer could hint at death, but it may just be a gift, so it doesn't establish that he died.

Answer: yes

Chapter 7 records that Malis Prydenridge was laid in the churchyard at Ostcombe, dead of a long wasting sickness. Nothing later says otherwise.

Answer: no

No record of Marald Corrford's death appears in the material. The latest information about him is that he moved to Ravenmere and did not return to Elmhaven, so he is presumably still alive.

Answer: yes

Excerpt 577 (Chapter 5) says a long wasting sickness took Nylia Corrford that summer and she was buried at Dunstead. Later excerpts only mention her in the past or in other contexts, and the record gives no sign she is alive again.

Answer: no

Chapter 22 records that Volia Brackick was laid in the churchyard at Kelford, dead of drowning in the flood. No later excerpt says otherwise, so she is not alive at the end of the record.

Answer: no

The rumor that Wenelle drowned (told by Ismira Stenson in Chapter 10) is contradicted by later events. Wenelle gave birth to Zavus in Chapter 12, took work as a chandler in Chapter 15, moved to Kelmere in Chapter 22, and had sons Febin (Chapter 25) and Madan (Chapter 37). In Chapter 37 she is still present and speaking.

Answer: yes

Matho Stenson has no recorded death. The only death claim is a rumor started by Pelde Stenson that he died of plague, and rumors aren't facts. In the latest excerpt (Chapter 37) he receives a bone compass, so he is still alive then.

Answer: yes

The only claim of Pelde Stenworth's death is a rumor, started by the second daughter of Rorald Lindmere, who had it from a peddler. Rumors are not facts. The record also shows Pelde Stenworth alive and active at the end, marrying Sebin Brackick at Torton in the last excerpt.

Answer: yes

The record gives no sign that Matho Stenson died. The only claim of his death is a rumor in Chapter 24, started by Pelde Stenson from a peddler, and rumors don't count as facts. In the last relevant entry (Chapter 37), Matho receives the bone compass that Ismira Stenson had owned, so he is still alive then.

Answer: yes

The only claim that Rorald Lindmere died is a rumor started by Movie Prydenridge, who got it from a peddler. A rumor is not a fact. The later excerpts show him still living and active: he lives in Yarlby, sorts letters by candlelight, and chats with his wife. Nothing in the record confirms his death.

Answer: yes

Rovus Prydenridge appears throughout the record with no death mentioned. Malis Prydenridge dies in Chapter 7, and a rumor about Rorald Lindmere's death is unconfirmed. Rovus is last seen in Chapter 37 as the father of Madan Prydenridge, and nothing later suggests he died.

Answer: yes

Ilrald Prydenridge was born in Chapter 19 and married in Chapter 33, moving to Torton. He appears again in Chapter 37 ("Ilrald Prydenridge and Pelde talked of nothing much"). No death is recorded for him anywhere in the material.

Answer: yes

No record of Yewyn Corrford's death appears in the material. She married Kadan Corrley at Kelmere, and later excerpts still show her alive, speaking with Kadan Corrley in Chapter 19. The only death recorded is that of Yedan Corrford, from a kick by a cart horse.

Answer: yes

Kassa Stenson appears in the latest chapters (Chapter 35, "Kassa remarked") and moved to Kelmere in Chapter 34. The only death claims are rumors about Ismira and Matho Stenson, and nothing says Kassa died. So Kassa is alive.

Answer: yes

There are two people named Bremira Corrford possibly: a daughter born to Kassa Brackick and Ulrald Corrford (chapter 13), who later married Zavus Prydenridge (chapter 25). The latest information shows her alive: chapter 26 she remarks about the river, and chapter 39 she receives a parcel with a silver chalice. No death is recorded for her (Yedan Corrford died, not Bremira).

Answer: yes

Istho Stenworth was born in Chapter 25. He appears in later chapters (33), humming a tune, counting coins, and complaining of an aching back in Chapter 37. Nothing in the record reports his death.

Answer: yes

Kassa Brackick appears throughout the record, and the latest mention (Chapter 39) shows her alive, agreeing in conversation. The only death mentioned is a rumor about Matho Stenson, not Kassa. Nothing indicates Kassa died.

Answer: yes

Taric Corrley is mentioned throughout the record, and the latest entries show him moving from Dungate back to Kelmere. Nothing in the material says he died, so he is alive at the end.

Answer: yes

The silver flute belonged to Ulrald Corrford (Excerpt 337), and later it went to Kassa Brackick (Excerpt 1235). No later excerpt shows it changing hands again. The silver chalice, which was Kassa Brackick's, went to Bremira Corrford, but that is a different object.

Answer: Kassa Brackick

The jade mirror starts with Rozek Stenenridge. It then passes back and forth between him and Luena Stenenridge. In the last mention, in Chapter 36, Rozek presses it into the hands of Luvie Prydenridge and takes nothing for it.

Answer: Luvie Prydenridge

Tracing the oak lantern: Luena Stenenridge kept it in a cedar box (Ch. 1), then pressed it into the hands of Rozek Stenenridge (Ch. 12). Rozek sent it by carrier to Rovus Prydenridge, who received it (Ch. 18). Wenelle Lindmere then won it from Rovus at cards, fairly, and kept it (Ch. 19). No later excerpt mentions it moving again.

Answer: Wenelle Lindmere

The copper chalice changed hands several times:

- It began with Luena Stenenridge.
- Rozek Stenenridge won it from her at cards, then Luena won it back, then Rozek won it again.
- Rozek then gave it to Luena.
- Luena sent it by carrier to Yera Stenworth, who received it.
- In the latest mention, Gadrek won it from Yera Stenworth at cards and kept it.

The record gives only the single name "Gadrek", with no surname.

Answer: Gadrek

The oak comb was among Isric Thornmere's possessions (Excerpt 357). Later, Isric sent the oak comb by carrier to Kassa Brackick, who received it safely (Excerpt 1313). No later excerpt mentions it moving again.

Answer: Kassa Brackick

The pewter dagger first belonged to Yewyn Haskick, who gave it to the youngest son of a Brackick. That son then sent it to Jotho Thornmere, who was to keep it. In the latest relevant passage, Yera Stenworth won the dagger from "Quiet Jotho" at cards and kept it. I'm taking "Quiet Jotho" to be Jotho Thornmere, since the record gives no other Jotho.

Answer: Yera Stenworth

Tracing the brass map: it belonged to Ismira Stenson (Excerpt 364), and she then gave it to Matho Stenson (Excerpt 964). No later excerpt shows it changing hands again. The amber map is a separate item and doesn't affect this.

Answer: Matho Stenson

The amber map changes hands several times in the record:

- Tatho Brackick owned it first, then sent it to Marald.
- It reached Ulrald Corrford, then Kassa Brackick, then Volan Stenworth.
- In Chapter 33, Volan Stenworth gave it to Rimor Corrford, which is the last mention of it.

Answer: Rimor Corrford

The silver chalice was last mentioned in Chapter 39. A parcel from Lura Haskick reached Bremira Corrford with the silver chalice inside, "now hers to keep." Earlier, it was among Kassa Brackick's possessions, so this is the latest transfer.

Answer: Bremira Corrford

The ivory lantern belonged to Ismira Stenson (Excerpt 378). Later, in Excerpt 1700, Ismira Stenson pressed the ivory lantern into the hands of Rimor Corrford and would take nothing for it. No later excerpt mentions it changing hands again.

Answer: Rimor Corrford

The bone compass passed through these holders in order:

1. Thizek Stenenridge sent it to Lura.
2. Lura Haskick sent it to Volan Stenworth.
3. Volan's wife won it from him at cards and kept it.
4. Kassa Brackick gave it to Ismira (Stenson).
5. It went from Ismira Stenson to Matho Stenson.
6. Matho Stenson sent it by parcel to Luvie Prydenridge, "now hers to keep."

The last transfer is the one in Chapter 39, so Luvie Prydenridge holds it at the end.

Answer: Luvie Prydenridge

The only record of who holds the ivory chalice is Excerpt 391, which says it belonged to Ludrek Prydenridge. Excerpt 457 says it passes to the holder's eldest living child on the holder's death. No excerpt reports Ludrek's death or any transfer, so he is still the latest known holder.

Answer: Ludrek Prydenridge

The silver flute belonged to Ulrald Corrford (Excerpt 337). Later it went to Kassa Brackick (Excerpt 1235). No later transfer is recorded, so Kassa Brackick is the current holder, and the holder immediately before was Ulrald Corrford.

Answer: Ulrald Corrford

The jade mirror started with Rozek Stenenridge, who gave it to Luena Stenenridge in chapter 5. Luena gave it back to Rozek in chapter 16. Rozek then pressed it into the hands of his wife, probably Luena, in chapter 16. In chapter 36, Rozek pressed it into the hands of Luvie Prydenridge, who is the latest holder. The person who held it immediately before Luvie was therefore Rozek.

Answer: Rozek Stenenridge

The oak lantern passed from Luena Stenenridge to Rozek Stenenridge, then Rozek sent it to Rovus Prydenridge. Wenelle Lindmere then won it from Rovus at cards and kept it, so she is the current holder, and Rovus held it immediately before her.

Answer: Rovus Prydenridge

The copper chalice changed hands in this order:

1. It belonged to Luena Stenenridge.
2. Rozek Stenenridge won it from Luena at cards.
3. Luena won it back from Rozek.
4. Rozek won it again.
5. Rozek gave it to Luena.
6. Luena sent it to Yera Stenworth, who received it.
7. Gadrek won it from Yera Stenworth at cards and kept it.

Gadrek is the latest holder, so the holder immediately before was Yera Stenworth.

Answer: Yera Stenworth

The oak comb was among the possessions of Isric Thornmere. Isric later sent it by carrier to Kassa Brackick, who received it safely. Kassa Brackick is therefore the current holder, and Isric Thornmere held it immediately before.

Answer: Isric Thornmere

The pewter dagger passed from Yewyn Haskick to the youngest son of a Brackick, and then, by parcel, to Jotho Thornmere. Yera Stenworth later won it from "Quiet Jotho" at cards and kept it, so Yera is the current holder. I take "Quiet Jotho" to be Jotho Thornmere. The holder just before Yera was therefore Jotho Thornmere.

Answer: Jotho Thornmere

The brass map first belonged to Ismira Stenson, who then gave it to Matho Stenson, its current holder. No later transfer is recorded, so the holder immediately before Matho was Ismira.

Answer: Ismira Stenson

The amber map passed through these holders in order: Tatho Brackick, Marald Corrford, Ulrald Corrford, Kassa Brackick, Volan Stenworth, and then Rimor Corrford. Rimor Corrford is the latest holder, so the one immediately before was Volan Stenworth.

Answer: Volan Stenworth

The silver chalice was first with Kassa Brackick (Excerpt 376). In Excerpt 1949, a parcel from Lura Haskick reached Bremira Corrford with the silver chalice inside, now hers to keep. Bremira Corrford is therefore the current holder, and Lura Haskick, who sent it, held it immediately before her. The material doesn't show how it passed from Kassa Brackick to Lura, but that doesn't change who held it last.

Answer: Lura Haskick

The ivory lantern belonged to Ismira Stenson, who later gave it to Rimor Corrford, its current holder. The record shows no other holder between them.

Answer: Ismira Stenson

The bone compass passed through these holders in order: Ulrald Corrford, Fenelle Lindmere, Thizek Stenenridge, Lura Haskick, Volan Stenworth, Volan's wife, Kassa Brackick, Ismira Stenson, Matho Stenson, and finally Luvie Prydenridge. The latest record says Matho Stenson sent it to Luvie Prydenridge, so Luvie is the current holder and Matho held it just before.

Answer: Matho Stenson

Movie Prydenridge's father is Rovus Prydenridge (Chapter 6). Rovus's father is Ludrek Prydenridge (Chapter 1: Ludrek and Malis had children including Rovus).

Answer: Ludrek Prydenridge

The material doesn't say who Kassa Brackick's mother is. Rimor Corrford's parents are Kassa Brackick and Ulrald Corrford, so his maternal grandmother would be Kassa's mother. The only related item is a rumor that Tatho Brackick secretly married Fewyn Stenworth. It doesn't say how Tatho is related to Kassa, and rumors aren't facts.

Answer: unknown

Madan Prydenridge's father is Rovus Prydenridge, whose parents are Ludrek Prydenridge and Malis Prydenridge. So the paternal grandmother is Malis Prydenridge.

Answer: Malis Prydenridge

Nerine Prydenridge's father is Rovus Prydenridge. Rovus's parents are Ludrek Prydenridge and Malis Prydenridge, so his mother, Nerine's paternal grandmother, is Malis Prydenridge.

Answer: Malis Prydenridge

The record names Iszek Brackick's mother as Dalis Stenworth and his father as Movus Brackick. It never says who Dalis Stenworth's parents are. The only Stenworth child tied to a mother is Isvie Stenworth, born to Luwyn Brackick, and nothing links Dalis to Luwyn or to anyone else as a daughter. So the maternal grandmother can't be determined from this material.

Answer: unknown

Istho Stenworth's father is Lurald Stenworth (son of Havus Stenworth and Fewyn Stenworth). The paternal grandmother is Lurald's mother, Fewyn Stenworth.

Answer: Fewyn Stenworth

Febin Prydenridge's father is Rovus Prydenridge, whose parents are Ludrek Prydenridge and Malis Prydenridge. So the paternal grandmother is Malis Prydenridge.

Answer: Malis Prydenridge

Ferald Stenworth's father is Lurald Stenworth (son of Havus Stenworth and Fewyn Stenworth). His mother is Luwyn Brackick. The paternal grandfather is therefore Havus Stenworth.

Answer: Havus Stenworth

Elra Corrford's parents are Fenelle Lindmere and Marald Corrford. Marald is the son of Yedan Corrford and Nylia Corrford, so he is Elra's father, and Elra's maternal grandfather would be Fenelle Lindmere's father.

The material does not say who Fenelle Lindmere's parents are, so the maternal grandfather is not given.

Answer: unknown

Bremira Corrford is the daughter of Kassa Brackick and Ulrald Corrford. Ulrald is the eldest son of Yedan Corrford and Nylia Corrford. So her paternal grandfather is Yedan Corrford.

Answer: Yedan Corrford

Kamira Stenenridge's parents are Movie Prydenridge and Thizek Stenenridge. Thizek is the eldest son of Rozek Stenenridge and Luena Stenenridge (Chapter 1). Since Thizek is Kamira's father, Rozek Stenenridge is her paternal grandfather.

Answer: Rozek Stenenridge

The record names Semor Brackick's parents as Yewyn Haskick and Tatho Brackick, so the maternal grandfather would be Yewyn Haskick's father. Tatho is the son of Nelan Brackick, which makes Nelan the paternal grandfather. The material never says who Yewyn's father is.

Answer: unknown

The record names Movus Brackick's parents as Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick. His maternal grandmother would therefore be Rinelle Corrley's mother. The material never mentions Rinelle's parents. Volia Brackick, Kadrek's mother, is his paternal grandmother, not his maternal one.

Answer: unknown

The material says Zavus Prydenridge's mother is Wenelle (Lindmere) and his father is Rovus Prydenridge. It never names Wenelle's father, so his maternal grandfather can't be determined.

Answer: unknown
